elements.quote: Social media has gained significant popularity in recent decades... As of February 2023, there were approximately 4.95 billion social media users worldwide... Oral diseases affect 3.5 billion of the worldwide population and cases a high burden of diseases... While there have been several studies investigating the impact of social media on dentistry, there is limited information available on the effectiveness of online interventions through social media aimed at preventing diseases and promoting oral health among laypeople.
elements.reason: The text describes the current state of knowledge regarding social media usage and oral health, and identifies the uncertainty/gap regarding the effectiveness of social media interventions for oral health promotion among laypeople.

elements.quote: Clinicians can benefit from familiarizing themselves with the interventions described in the literature and evaluating the reported outcomes. This will enable them to make informed decisions using the cost-effective and accessible tool of social media. Therefore, the objective of this study is to systematically review the current evidence regarding social media-based interventions designed for disease prevention and oral health promotion among laypeople.
elements.reason: The text explains the importance of the review by noting that clinicians need to understand these interventions to make informed decisions, justifying the need for the systematic review.
The manuscript does not state that this is an update or replication of a previous systematic review, nor does it indicate that similar systematic reviews exist that require differentiation.

The review focuses on social media as a tool/platform for delivery, rather than evaluating the mechanism of action of a specific clinical intervention (e.g., a drug or specific therapy). The intervention is the delivery method itself.

The manuscript does not present a logic model, and the intervention (social media use for health promotion) is not described as a complex intervention requiring a logic model in the context of this review's rationale.

elements.quote: This systematic review aims to address the following PIO question: 'What is the effect of social media on prevention and promotion of oral health compared with conventional strategies among lay people of any age without disability or systematic diseases?'
elements.reason: The review explicitly states its objective using a PIO (Population, Intervention, Outcome) framework.

elements.quote: This systematic review aims to address the following PIO question: 'What is the effect of social media on prevention and promotion of oral health compared with conventional strategies among lay people of any age without disability or systematic diseases?'. The review encompasses (P) laypeople from diverse backgrounds... The focus is on (I) social media-based interventions... The desired outcomes include (O) any changes in oral health status, knowledge, beliefs, and attitudes...
elements.reason: The review is of intervention effects and explicitly states the planned comparisons and components using a PIO framework.

elements.quote: The review encompasses (P) laypeople from diverse backgrounds, including different age groups, genders, socioeconomic statuses, ethnicities without any disability or systematic diseases. The focus is on (I) social media-based interventions that employ a group approach for information dissemination. The desired outcomes include (O) any changes in oral health status, knowledge, beliefs, and attitudes resulting from social media interventions. This includes short and long-term effects, regardless of the duration of follow-up. The full-text articles from 2012 to 2023 focus on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-randomized trials and field trials were included in the current study.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly defines the PIO components (Population, Intervention, Outcomes), study designs (RCTs, quasi-randomized trials, field trials), and mentions follow-up (short and long-term effects).

elements.quote: The full-text articles from 2012 to 2023... Studies that... were published in languages other than English were excluded. The conference proceedings, editorials, commentaries, review articles, pilot studies and all the studies that assessed the quality of the content of social media were excluded.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the dissemination year range (2012-2023), language restriction (English), and publication status/type exclusions (conference proceedings, editorials, etc.).
There is no evidence that the review excluded studies specifically because outcomes were not measured versus not reported; this is a conditional requirement that does not apply here.
